finding: Pilot: OpenRouter switched hosts mid-batch (Qwen served in 4-bit). Every OpenRouter model is now pinned to one fp8 host with no fallback.
Mistral Small 3.2 fell into repetition loops at temperature 0 (2 of 10 pilot conversations). Customer switched to Mistral Small 2603 before any study run; loops are flagged and re-run.
The simulated customer sometimes goes off-script (pilot task 7 asked to cancel extra bookings). Failed conversations need a customer-error audit before blaming the agent.
Pass rate 45/60 at every level. Haiku broke a rule in 1 of 41 changes at H0 and none above, so the rails had little to fix; most failures are missed actions.
Clearer rules and code checks lifted DeepSeek from 41/60 (H0) to 45/60 (H1) and 49/60 (H2); rule violations fell from 6 at H0 to 0.
In the harness pilot the H3 verifier caught a real error: an upgrade charged $1,182 when the customer had confirmed $662.
Parasail rate-limited OpenRouter's shared pool and refused every call; Qwen moved to DeepInfra fp8 before any study data.
Pass rate 46/60 (H0), 46/60 (H1), 44/60 (H2), 43/59 (H3): flat within noise. Qwen broke no rule even at H0 and no gate ever fired, so the rails had nothing to fix.

Qwen is the priciest cheap model here: about $0.02 per conversation, roughly 3x Haiku (which benefits from prompt caching) and 10x DeepSeek, because it writes long replies (~630 output tokens per message).

Qwen sometimes returned an empty reply (5-12 times per 60 conversations); tau2 restarts the conversation. One H3 conversation failed all 3 tries and is excluded as infrastructure_error (H3 scored on 59).

Sonnet H0 on the fixed 15-task half (core_15, 30 conversations): 19/30, the same as DeepSeek H0 and below DeepSeek H2 (24/30) and Haiku H1 (26/30) on the same tasks, at about $0.11 per conversation (~60x DeepSeek).

Correction: an earlier note blamed 3 Sonnet failures on comma formatting. tau2's substring scorer already strips commas; the 3 failures are real omissions (Sonnet never stated the total of $1,628 or the $1,000 certificate sum).

Grader audit: 18 conversations made every right change but failed the 'tell the customer' check; in none of them did the fact appear in another format (number words, decimals). All 18 are real omissions.

Hand audit of 26 failed conversations (2 per condition, seeded): 16 agent errors, 7 customer errors (27%, 95% range 14-46%), 3 unclear. Customer errors: invented IDs, refusing the payment its script prefers, accepting a price over its budget, asking for extra cancellations.

In task 7 the simulated customer asked to cancel two reservations its script never mentions in 9 of 26 conversations, across all models. Task 39 (cancel all, including one with no refund) failed for every model: agents cancel 2 of 3.

The one over-block (H3, task 17) was a gate limit: three changes sent in one message were each checked against the database before the earlier ones ran, so the bag count looked wrong. The agent redid them one at a time and they passed; the conversation failed because the customer refused its preferred gift card.
